title: OSU Moves Moritz College of Law Downtown Into Huntington Tower
author: CRE News Staff
excerpt: Ohio State will move Moritz College of Law into downtown's historic Huntington Bank tower under a 30-year lease with an option to buy, opening fall 2029.
answer_summary: Ohio State University will move its Moritz College of Law from campus into downtown Columbus's historic Huntington Bank building at 17 South High Street, under a 30-year lease with Downtown Columbus Inc. that includes an option to purchase. The law school expects to open there in fall 2029.

body:
Ohio State University will move its Moritz College of Law from campus into downtown Columbus's historic Huntington Bank building at 17 South High Street, under a 30-year lease with Downtown Columbus Inc. that includes an option to purchase. The law school expects to open there in fall 2029.

## What OSU announced today

University and city leaders gathered in the atrium of the old bank building at High and Broad streets Monday to confirm the move. OSU President Ravi Bellamkonda, Moritz Dean Kent Barnett, Columbus Mayor Andrew Ginther, Huntington Bank's Central Ohio region president Sue Zazon, and Downtown Columbus Inc. president Alex Fischer all spoke, according to [Columbus Underground](https://columbusunderground.com/osu-to-move-law-school-downtown-bw1/) and [WOSU Public Media](https://www.wosu.org/politics-government/2026-09-14/ohio-state-university-to-move-moritz-college-of-law-to-downtown-columbus-by-fall-2029). "This marks the beginning of the best town-gown relationship in America," Fischer said, according to Columbus Underground's report of the event.

The building sits directly across from the Ohio Statehouse, next door to Huntington's current headquarters tower — a location OSU says puts law students within walking distance of the Statehouse, Columbus City Hall, the Ohio Supreme Court, and the state and county courts and law firms clustered downtown.

## Inside the deal: a 30-year lease with an option to buy

Downtown Columbus Inc. — the nonprofit formerly known as the Columbus Downtown Development Corporation — will lease roughly 200,000 square feet in the 13-story building to OSU for 30 years, with an option to purchase the property later. That is longer than the "at least 20 years" floor OSU's own Board of Trustees set when it authorized lease negotiations. The trustees took that vote at their June 2026 meeting, as [NBC4](https://www.nbc4i.com/news/local-news/ohio-state-university/ohio-state-eyes-lease-of-huntington-skyscraper-in-downtown-columbus/) and [Hoodline](https://hoodline.com/2026/06/ohio-state-to-plant-flag-in-capitol-square-s-historic-huntington-tower/) reported at the time, and the [full board record is public](https://trustees.osu.edu/meeting/2026/6/bot-public-june-2026). Back in June, OSU had not said publicly what the space would be used for; Monday's announcement is the first confirmation that Moritz, not another department, is the anchor tenant.

## From bank lobby to law school: the renovation plan

DCI will lead the building's renovation. The main floor — the old bank's lobby — becomes event space and a common area. Upper floors will be gutted and rebuilt as classrooms, a law library, and faculty offices. Huntington will keep a street-level bank branch in the building, and one floor is set aside for possible use by Ohio State's Wexner Medical Center. Moritz would occupy nearly the rest of the tower. No renovation budget has been made public in any of the reporting reviewed for this story.

## How DCI ended up owning a bank tower

The building, once known as the Capitol Square Building, was one of three Huntington-owned buildings DCI agreed to buy in 2024, part of the bank's move to consolidate downtown into its newer headquarters tower a block away. [Colliers](https://www.colliers.com/en/news/columbus/downtown-columbus-inc-will-buy-trio-of-huntington-buildings) covered that acquisition at the time. Huntington National Bank sold this particular tower to DCI in January 2025 for more than $4.5 million, per NBC4's reporting. A three-year-old office sale for $4.5 million and a 30-year, roughly 200,000-square-foot anchor lease to a state university are very different kinds of transactions: the first priced an empty building, the second prices what DCI can do with it filled.

## A downtown return for Moritz, not a first

Moritz's move isn't unprecedented for the law school. Ohio State's law program opened in 1891 with 33 students in the basement of the old Franklin County Courthouse. It moved to campus at Page Hall in 1903 and later to Drinko Hall, its current building, where it has stayed for decades. Fall 2029 would mark the school's first sustained downtown presence in more than a century.

## What's still unresolved

No party has released a total project cost. None of the coverage reviewed names a construction timeline beyond the fall 2029 opening target, and it's not yet clear what happens to Drinko Hall or the law school's current campus space once Moritz relocates. The move adds a large, long-term institutional tenant to Capitol Square at a moment when downtown Columbus has multiple office buildings converting to other uses — CREN has [previously covered](https://columbusrealestatenews.com/blog/downtown-columbus-office-tower-wins-2026-redevelopment-of-the-year) another downtown office tower redevelopment recognized this year. Whether a law school of Moritz's size can do for daytime foot traffic on Capitol Square what office workers used to is a question the market will answer over time, not something this announcement itself proves.

For more on downtown Columbus development, see CREN's [area coverage](https://columbusrealestatenews.com/areas/downtown-columbus) and [development coverage](https://columbusrealestatenews.com/topics/development).
